title: The issuer URL comes from a file anyone on the box can write
description:
THE INPUT IS UNTRUSTED AND THE OUTPUT IS AN OUTBOUND REQUEST. oidc.rs reads ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json and ~/.azure/* and takes `iss` out of a token whose signature has not been checked -- that is the whole point of the bead, the signature check is what is missing. Discovery then turns that string into a URL hired fetches. So anyone who can write the user's home directory chooses a URL the daemon requests, with the daemon's network position and its ambient credentials to any host that trusts its source address.

This is not hypothetical for a desktop daemon: the cache file is exactly what a first-stage payload can write, and 'hired fetched it' may be more interesting to an attacker than anything hired then issues.

CONSTRAINTS TO APPLY, all cheap and all in the fetch path:
- https only. An `iss` of http://, file://, or anything else is refused before a request is made.
- No redirect following, or at most one and only to the same host. A redirect is the standard way to turn an allowed URL into a disallowed one.
- A total timeout and a response size cap, so a hostile endpoint cannot hold a request open or stream indefinitely. This is why persona-qbnm.7.1 lists them as requirements.
- The discovery document's own `issuer` field MUST equal the `iss` it was fetched for. OIDC Discovery requires this, and it is also what stops a redirected or substituted document naming somebody else's keys.
- The jwks_uri from the discovery document must be on the same host as the issuer. The spec does not require it; the alternative is letting an attacker-chosen document point the key fetch anywhere.

WORTH CONSIDERING AND DECIDING EXPLICITLY: an issuer allowlist. A desktop has one or two work IdPs, not an open set. A constraint here -- 'hire fetches JWKS only for issuers the operator enrolled' -- would delete this whole category, and it is the kind of thing persona-08sz's enrollment record exists to hold. That is a cheaper answer than hardening the fetch, if the operator is willing to name their IdP once.
acceptance_criteria: An iss naming a non-https scheme, a redirect to another host, or a discovery document whose issuer field disagrees, each produce no fetch and no evidence; the decision on an issuer allowlist is recorded either way.
